---
title: "Profitable Banks, Unprofitable Politics"
date: "2010-11-17"
categories: ["Economics", "Monetary Policy", "Politics"]
---

I have an op-ed in today’s [WSJ](http://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424052748704312504575617933648395028.html?mod=asia_opinion "WSJ") arguing that the government and opposition’s attacks on the banks are a pointless diversion. [Saul Eslake](http://www.theage.com.au/business/rate-must-rise-a-bit-20101116-17w1e.html "Saul Eslake") makes similar arguments in today’s Age. After yesterday’s RBA Board minutes destroyed the politicians’ case against the banks, the best Joe Hockey can come up with is [this](http://www.theaustralian.com.au/national-affairs/rserve-bank-of-australia-argues-big-banks-case/story-fn59niix-1225954656201 "this"):

> *Mr Hockey said the minutes had contemplated the banks going further than the official rise but didn’t contemplate the banks going as far as they did.*

**UPDATE**: I have another op-ed in the Business section of [The Australian](http://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/attacks-on-banks-overlook-effect-of-strong-growth-prospects/story-e6frg8zx-1225955207724 "The Australian").
